title: Find repeats in code, then by meaning
statement: Find repeated questions with a code check for near-identical wording, which gives the same answer every run, and list a judge's same-meaning pairs separately, at lower confidence.
example: A code check gave the same answer every run but missed a same-meaning pair whose word overlap was 0.5, below its 0.85 bar.
detail: The judge's calls on repeated questions flip-flopped between runs and flagged unlike items, such as a short constructed response and a sequence item, as redundant. A code detector (same interaction type and question-stem token-set Jaccard >= 0.85) was fully reproducible and matched the cases the judge got right without its false positives, but missed same-meaning pairs with a token overlap of 0.5. The hybrid keeps the code detector as the floor and adds the judge's structured same-meaning pairs as a separate, lower-confidence list; the code detector was validated on a 14-item sample x3.
against: Validated on a small sample: 'full-course re-measure is the real confirmation.' (shadow-bench, git commit 69d56ab, line 49).

evidence.quote: same interaction type + question-stem token-set Jaccard >= 0.85. Fully reproducible; matches the cases the LLM got right (identical / near-identical stems) without its false positives (e.g. an SCR + a sequence item wrongly flagged as "redundant").
The deterministic detector (#30) is high-precision + zero-variance but misses SEMANTIC duplicates … token overlap 0.5, below the 0.85 bar
The old LLM approach caught those but flip-flopped
The LLM-only subset is surfaced separately as `semantic_repetitive_items` (lower confidence) so consumers
